transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... the men down at the domino table, and sometimes the announcer on the radio, they've been giving these little messages meant for me. My wife, she says it is just talk and I shouldn't pay it no mind. But I know they are warning me to be careful. So, that's what brings me in today.
Aside from these messages you've been hearing, have you been feeling unusually high-spirited or energetic, or perhaps very sad and hopeless lately?

Well, I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad. But... there are weeks when I wake up feeling just real bright and important. I get all this energy, and I end up laughing loud and talking real fast to folks. 

The only thing is, if somebody tries to slow me down, or if they question what I'm doing... well, I can get pretty sharp with them.
Are you still hearing these messages from the radio and the men at the table even during the times when you aren't feeling that high-spirited energy?

Yes, sir, I do. Like... well, there was a quiet month not too long ago. I was sleeping normal, getting my regular rest, and I wasn't full of all them big plans or that fast energy. But even during that quiet time, I still heard my friend out on the porch, and I still knew that radio was speaking directly to me. So, yes, it still happens even when I'm just feeling regular.
When you have these experiences, do you ever find that your thoughts get jumbled up or that it becomes difficult for you to keep your train of thought organized?

Well, yes, sometimes they do. It's like... my mind just takes off running. I'll be thinking about the church choir, and then suddenly I'm thinking about a baseball game, and then what needs fixing around the house, and then my friend... and it just goes back and forth so fast. I can't even hold onto one single thought long enough to explain it right to anybody. It all just gets tangled up together.
During those times when you feel that high energy and talk fast, do you feel like you need much less sleep than usual, or do you find yourself needing to sleep more?

Well, it's definitely much less. On those nights, I might only sleep for maybe two or three hours. Then I'll just get right up, way before daylight, feeling completely ready to work just like I had a full night of rest. I just don't seem to need it when I get like that.
During the times when you are not feeling that high energy, do you ever experience periods of deep sadness or hopelessness that last for two weeks or more?

No, sir, I can't say I do. I mean, everybody gets a little down now and then, but not like what you're saying. I don't get stuck in no deep sadness or nothing like that for weeks on end. It's mostly just the fast energy times or the regular times for me.
